artifact_search_note: FRANK_ARCHITECTURE.claycode.json was not located by repository search and expected-path fetch returned 404; current FRANK directives and mesh feedback were used provisionally without fabrication.

items.frank_statement: Model or learned-state output must not itself confer external effect authority; effectful host access requires an external authority/capability boundary.
items.counterhypothesis: Ambient host FFI plus process sandboxing is sufficient; a typed capability gateway adds complexity without material safety gain.
items.falsifier: Representative FFI/system-effect tests show the explicit capability boundary can be bypassed as easily as ambient access, or provides no measurable containment/audit advantage.
independent_checks: Wasmtime/WASI primary documentation describes capability-scoped host access and absence of ambient built-in system calls in WebAssembly/WASI-style execution.
adversarial_checks: Future APP-08 must attempt file/process/network access without capability grants, including child/FFI equivalents.
items.reason: Independent implementation architecture supports capability-scoped host interfaces as a valid safety mechanism. This does not prove the final ClayCode gateway API or implementation correct.
items.claycode_action: Retain explicit capability/effect boundary; test it at ABI/FFI level rather than encode authority in model-readable text.

items.frank_statement: FRANK should be modeled as a hierarchical multiscale recurrent loop-of-loops and ClayCode should represent loop identity, timescale, budget, dynamics, interventions and rollback.
items.counterhypothesis: Ordinary persistent event-driven orchestration explains the useful behavior; recurrent dynamical mathematics adds no material predictive or control value.
items.falsifier: Matched H1/H2 replay shows loop-specific state/readouts/interventions do not improve prediction, control, diagnosis or recovery over a simpler event-driven representation.
adversarial_checks: Current run intentionally did not treat cross-branch repetition of the owner-distributed hypothesis as independent support.
items.reason: This run established parser-surface closure evidence only; it did not execute the loop-dynamics hypothesis. ClayCode must preserve representability and testability without promoting the mechanism as truth.
items.claycode_action: Use existing record/tensor/intervention/receipt primitives for the first executable LoopDynamicsReadout; add semantics only if that concrete program cannot be represented or lowered.

items.frank_statement: A useful Ubuntu lowering path may use native code and/or WASM/WASI with typed host interop.
items.counterhypothesis: Direct native Ubuntu lowering/FFI is simpler, faster and easier to debug; WASM/WASI adds an unnecessary boundary for the first release.
items.falsifier: Ubuntu application-suite benchmarks show WASM/WASI materially worsens latency, FFI coverage, debugging or resource control without compensating isolation/portability benefits.
independent_checks: WebAssembly Component Model/WIT primary specifications provide typed import/export interfaces and canonical lift/lower concepts.
Wasmtime/WASI primary documentation provides a capability-oriented execution boundary.
adversarial_checks: Do not infer target suitability from interface elegance; require APP-01..APP-10 execution and cost receipts on Ubuntu.
items.reason: WASM/WASI is independently supported as a viable typed host-boundary pattern, but evidence does not establish it as the mandatory or best first backend for FRANK v0.1.
items.claycode_action: Keep native and WASM/WASI as competing lowering targets; choose by Ubuntu execution evidence, not architecture preference.

items.frank_statement: FRANK v0.1 requires representable/replayable adaptive visual learner version, provenance tier, confidence/open-set, candidate promotion/rollback and resource-budget state.
items.counterhypothesis: Some of these fields may be implementable entirely in host/runtime state without first-class ClayCode semantics.
items.falsifier: H1-to-H2 differential implementation demonstrates equivalent replay/provenance/rollback semantics with a smaller existing ClayCode representation and no semantic escape hatch.
adversarial_checks: Treat the directive as a release contract, not independent scientific evidence for any particular classifier architecture.
items.reason: The requirement is owner-fixed for the product, while the minimal language representation and optimal learner mechanism remain research-gated.
items.claycode_action: Guarantee expressibility of required state/transition receipts using existing typed records/version/provenance primitives before adding dedicated learner syntax.
